sum: A short trek from Silgadhi in Doti up to the rolling 3,000 m grasslands of Khaptad National Park, with wide views of Api and Saipal and almost no other foreign visitors.

guide.note: The Nepal Tourism Board has required foreign trekkers in protected areas to hire a licensed guide since April 2023, though checks on the trail are inconsistent and rare this far west. A guide is still worth having here: there are few signs on the plateau, mist comes down quickly over the meadows, and beds and meals need arranging in advance.

access: Fly from Kathmandu to Dhangadhi in the far-western Terai, then drive seven to nine hours into the hills to Silgadhi in Doti. Buses and shared jeeps cover the same road. A jeep track continues from Silgadhi to the park gate at Jhigrana.

photo.a: A trekker with a backpack walks away along a stone-paved path across green rolling grassland towards a low hill, under large white clouds.
photo.c: The stone path across the Khaptad grasslands

includes: lodge, homestay or tent nights and meals on the trek
Kathmandu–Dhangadhi flights and road transport in most packages (confirm)

permits.name: Khaptad National Park entry permit
permits.where: At the park entry post on the way in, or in advance at the national parks counter in the Tourist Service Centre, Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu.

transportText: Flights between Kathmandu and Dhangadhi both ways
transportExtra: jeeps between Dhangadhi and the trailheads
tips: Buy supplies in Dhangadhi or Silgadhi and carry snacks and some staples up with you.
Bring a warm sleeping bag. Nights at 3,000 m are cold even in May, and lodge bedding is thin.
Alcohol, tobacco and the killing of animals are not allowed in the zone around the ashram. Follow the rule, and ask before you bring meat up.
Carry small notes; nobody on the plateau can change large bills.
The park fee is disputed between sources, and some agencies also issue a TIMS card for Khaptad. Carry extra cash for the gate and let your agency decide on the card.

days.note: North across the Terai and up into the hills on the Dadeldhura road, then east down to the Seti river at Dipayal and up to the ridge-top bazaar of Silgadhi. Visit the Shaileshwari temple in the evening if you arrive in time.

A steady climb along a ridge of farms and oak forest, now followed for much of the way by a jeep track; many people ride it and start walking at the park gate instead. Park staff at Jhigrana issue the entry permit.

days.t: Jhigrana to Khaptad by way of Bichpani
days.note: A sustained climb through oak, rhododendron and bamboo to the rest stop at Bichpani, then easier walking as the forest gives way to the first meadows. Published times for this day vary a lot, and slower groups break it with a night at Bichpani.

Walk a loop of the meadows: the Tribeni temple at the meeting of three streams, Khaptad Baba's ashram and the small lake of Khaptad Daha. Sahashra Linga, the highest ground in the park at about 3,200 m, is a longer outing; ask park staff for the way.
Back the way you came, quicker downhill. With an early start you can meet a jeep at the gate and reach Silgadhi the same evening, which shortens tomorrow's drive.
A long day back down to the plains by way of Silgadhi and Dipayal. Flights to Kathmandu leave Dhangadhi through the day, but book for the following morning in case the road is slow.
